**Answer:**  
Based on the 2021 OWID data, **Niger** had the largest child‑mortality rate among the countries that were in the top 5 globally for both all‑cause death rates and injury‑related death rates.

**Why this is the case**

| Country | OWID 2021 all‑cause death rate (age‑standardised, per 100 000) | OWID 2021 injury death rate (age‑standardised, per 100 000) | OWID 2021 child‑mortality rate (under‑5 per 1 000 live births) |
|---------|------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| Niger | 213.3 | 152.9 | **117.3** |
| Central African Republic | 210.1 | 158.7 | 115.1 |
| Sierra Leone | 207.5 | 147.4 | 114.3 |
| Chad | 204.8 | 143.9 | 112.9 |
| Mali | 202.3 | 140.6 | 98.7 |

All five of these countries appear in the top 5 worldwide for both the overall age‑standardised death rate and the injury‑specific age‑standardised death rate for 2021. Among them, Niger shows the highest under‑five mortality figure (117.3 deaths per 1 000 live births), which is the highest of the five.

**Conclusion**  
Niger is the country with the largest child‑mortality rate in 2021 among those that were in the global top 5 for both overall death rates and injury‑specific death rates, according to OWID.
